subject: Mathematics
name: Mathematics, Year 7
placeName: Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia, Tasmania, Australian Capital Territory and Northern Territory

points.title: Square numbers and square roots
points.brief: A square number is a number times itself, such as 7² = 49, and the square root undoes it, so √49 = 7. A root that is not whole lies between two whole numbers, so √43 is between 6 and 7.

points.title: Prime factorisation with index notation
points.brief: Any whole number above 1 can be written as a product of primes using a factor tree, then in index form, such as 72 = 2³ × 3².

points.title: Expanded notation with powers of 10
points.brief: Place value can be written with powers of 10, such as 4305 = 4 × 10³ + 3 × 10² + 5 × 10⁰.

points.title: Equivalent fractions and simplest form
points.brief: Multiplying or dividing the top and bottom of a fraction by the same number gives an equivalent fraction, and dividing by the highest common factor gives simplest form.

points.title: Converting fractions, decimals and percentages
points.brief: Switching between forms, such as 3/4 = 0.75 = 75%, and placing fractions, including negative ones, on a number line.

points.title: Rounding decimals
points.brief: Rounding a decimal to a given number of places by looking at the next digit, and estimating to check an answer is reasonable.

points.title: Adding and subtracting fractions
points.brief: Fractions with different denominators are added or subtracted by first rewriting them over a common denominator, including mixed numbers.

points.title: Multiplying and dividing fractions
points.brief: Multiply fractions by multiplying tops and bottoms, and divide by multiplying by the reciprocal of the second fraction.

points.title: Percentage of a quantity
points.brief: Finding a percentage of an amount by turning the percentage into a fraction or decimal and multiplying, such as 15% of $80 = $12.

points.title: Ordering integers on a number line
points.brief: Integers are whole numbers that can be negative, zero or positive, and numbers further right on the number line are larger, so −2 > −5.

points.title: Adding and subtracting integers
points.brief: Adding a negative is the same as subtracting, and subtracting a negative is the same as adding, so 3 − (−4) = 7.

points.title: Simplifying ratios
points.brief: A ratio compares quantities in the same units and is simplified by dividing each part by their highest common factor, so 12 to 18 is 2 to 3.

points.title: Dividing a quantity in a ratio
points.brief: To share an amount in a ratio, add the parts, find one part, then multiply, so $60 shared 2 to 3 gives $24 and $36.

points.title: Discounts and price increases
points.brief: Finding a sale price after a percentage discount, or a new price after a percentage increase, such as adding 10% GST.

points.title: Writing algebraic expressions
points.brief: Turning words into algebra with variables, numbers and brackets, writing 3n for 3 × n, such as 5 more than double a number as 2n + 5.

points.title: Substituting into formulas
points.brief: Replacing each variable in a formula with its value and following the order of operations, such as finding P = 2l + 2w when l = 5 and w = 3.

points.title: Tables of values from a rule
points.brief: A rule such as y = 2x + 1, or a growing pattern of shapes, makes a table of values by putting in each x.

points.title: Solving one-step equations
points.brief: Solve an equation by doing the inverse operation to both sides, so x + 7 = 12 gives x = 5 and 4x = 28 gives x = 7.

points.title: Solving two-step equations
points.brief: Undo the operations in reverse order, adding or subtracting first, then dividing, so 3x + 5 = 20 gives x = 5. Check by substituting back.

points.title: Plotting points on the Cartesian plane
points.brief: Points are plotted as (x, y), across then up or down, in all four quadrants, and points from a rule can show a straight-line pattern.

points.title: Reading graphs of real data
points.brief: Reading a graph of real data, such as temperature over a day, to describe how one variable changes as the other changes.

points.title: Area of triangles and parallelograms
points.brief: A parallelogram's area is base times perpendicular height, and a triangle's is half of base times perpendicular height.

points.title: Volume of rectangular and triangular prisms
points.brief: The volume of a right prism is the area of its cross-section times its length, so a rectangular prism is length times width times height, in cubic units such as cm³.

points.title: Radius, diameter, circumference and pi
points.brief: The diameter is twice the radius, and for every circle the circumference divided by the diameter is the same number, pi, about 3.14.

points.title: Corresponding and alternate angles
points.brief: When a transversal crosses parallel lines, corresponding angles (an F shape) are equal and alternate angles (a Z shape) are equal.

points.title: Co-interior angles
points.brief: When a transversal crosses parallel lines, co-interior angles (a C shape) add to 180°, and they show whether lines are parallel.

points.title: Angle sum of a triangle
points.brief: The angles inside a triangle add to 180°, so the third angle is 180° minus the other two.

points.title: Angle sum of polygons
points.brief: A polygon splits into triangles from one vertex, so a quadrilateral's angles add to 360° and an n-sided polygon's to (n − 2) × 180°.

points.title: Classifying triangles
points.brief: Triangles are named by their sides, as equilateral, isosceles or scalene, and by their angles, as acute, right or obtuse.

points.title: Classifying quadrilaterals
points.brief: Squares, rectangles, rhombuses, parallelograms, trapeziums and kites are told apart by their parallel sides, equal sides, angles and diagonals.

points.title: Nets and views of objects
points.brief: A three-dimensional object can be drawn in two dimensions as a net, as front, side and top views, or in perspective, and each shows different things.

points.title: Translations and reflections
points.brief: A translation slides each point, such as 3 right and 2 down, and a reflection in the x-axis changes (x, y) to (x, −y).

points.title: Rotations about a point
points.brief: A rotation turns a shape through an angle about a fixed point, such as 90° clockwise about the origin.

points.title: Algorithms that sort shapes
points.brief: An algorithm is a set of steps and yes or no decisions, such as a flowchart asking whether a shape has 4 sides, that sorts shapes into groups.

points.title: Discrete and continuous data
points.brief: Discrete numerical data is counted, such as the number of pets, and continuous data is measured, such as height.

points.title: Mean, median, mode and range
points.brief: The mean is the total divided by the count, the median is the middle value in order, the mode is the most common, and the range is highest minus lowest.

points.title: Choosing a measure of centre
points.brief: An outlier pulls the mean towards it, so the median often describes the centre better when data has extreme values.

points.title: Stem-and-leaf plots
points.brief: A stem-and-leaf plot splits each value into a stem and a leaf, keeping every value while showing the shape of the data.

points.title: Shape of a distribution
points.brief: A distribution can be symmetric or skewed, and can have clusters, gaps and outliers, which a display makes easy to see.

points.title: Sample spaces and probability
points.brief: The sample space lists every possible outcome, such as 1 to 6 for a die. With equally likely outcomes, the probability of an event is the number of favourable outcomes divided by the total, from 0 to 1.

points.title: Expected and relative frequency
points.brief: Relative frequency is how often an event happened in trials divided by the number of trials, and expected frequency is probability times the number of trials.

points.title: Experiments and theory
points.brief: Results of a chance experiment vary, but with many trials the relative frequency gets closer to the theoretical probability.
